analysis: All three changed files are documentation only, and no source code was supplied. The one item to carry forward is the new prefix-cache.md paragraph (head lines ~129-153), which says SSD prefix-cache eligibility defaults on for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp (PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel), with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. This extends the default-on at-rest cache surface covered by T-041 and SEC-035. T-041 describes default-on for eligible CBv2 models with a per-donation gate, HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL and a KEK purge. It does not list GLM or the new native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1 layout. The doc says GLM is outside the registered coordinator serving models, so the cross-tenant TTFT oracle is likely limited to local use. I did not flag this: the supplied evidence is prose only, with no code establishing that the controls (HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, a verified load hash) are bypassed. If the GLM code is in a later batch, check that GLM full-state files use the HMAC tags, the authenticated cacheSalt, the 30-minute TTL cap and the load-hash gate. Also consider adding the GLM layout to T-041's affected scope. inference.md (head ~1239-1263, 1273-1321) describes MiMo changes: tool-schema restoration with rejection of reserved metadata, bounded audio and visual decode with size checks before allocation, and memory-backed video with no disk write. These reduce risk or are neutral, and the claims are unverified without source. model-registry.md adds a GLM discovery quotation note with no tokenizer fallback, which is neutral.
